deeperExplanation.question: What if the conversation really is an interview?
deeperExplanation.answer: An interview still has a practical purpose: help the other person understand your experience and decide whether it fits the role. You can prepare facts and examples, then answer the question actually asked. The useful shift is from how impressive am I being to what do they need to understand here. The situation can remain important while the immediate speaking task becomes smaller and more concrete.

sections.narration:
Welcome. Today we are exploring Drop Performance Mode. A colleague asks how your project is going. You begin arranging the answer to sound intelligent. Before you have shared the update, you are listening to yourself as though you are being interviewed on a stage.

In this session, we will notice impression management, identify the listener's need, and share one useful piece. I will explain the idea, show a visual example, and invite you to try it in a small experience of your own. You can ask me a question or switch to reading at any point. We will finish by choosing what, if anything, you want to take into a real conversation.

sections.narration: Performance mode makes the impression you create the main task. Conversation then becomes two jobs: share the message and supervise how impressive you sound. Today we will move the task back to the exchange. Ask what the listener needs to understand, and offer one useful piece. Your delivery can still have expression and care. It does not have to carry a whole demonstration of your competence.

A colleague asks how your project is going. You begin arranging the answer to sound intelligent. Before you have shared the update, you are listening to yourself as though you are being interviewed on a stage.

You may feel that reducing performance effort will make you careless or dull. Test that belief in a small setting. An answer can be plain and still useful. Clear ordinary language often gives the other person more room to respond. The difference is not between excellent and bad speaking; it is between a shared task and an examination you are administering to yourself.

sections.narration: You are not required to feel casual in a serious meeting. You can feel nervous and still serve the purpose of the exchange. A warm or playful tone is welcome when it fits, but being funny is not another requirement. A changed, unchanged or uncertain experience is information, not a grade. You do not have to report relief for this attempt to count as exploration.

sections.narration: Before one conversation, write a five-word purpose such as explain the next useful step. Use that as your task, then reflect briefly afterwards. During focused practice, you can deliberately explore this one tool. In an everyday conversation, give most of your attention to the message and the other person. A familiar support can be available if it helps; you do not have to monitor the tool throughout the exchange.
